'''John Alfred Cowan Jr.''' (born April 9, 1975) is an American politician and neurosurgeon. A [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]], he is the member-elect for [[Georgia's 11th congressional district]] in the [[United States House of Representatives]]. He was previously a candidate for the [[Georgia's 14th congressional district|14th district]] in the [[2020 United States House of Representatives elections in Georgia#District 14|2020 House elections]], but lost the primary to [[Marjorie Taylor Greene]].

==Early life and education==
John Cowan was born on April 9, 1975.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.legistorm.com/person/bio/369543/John_Alfred_Cowan_Jr_.html|title=John Cowan - R Georgia, 11th, Candidate - Biography &#124; LegiStorm|website=www.legistorm.com}}</ref> Cowan is from [[Cartersville, Georgia]]. He graduated from [[Cartersville High School]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://readv3.com/2020/03/doctor-in-the-house-with-john-cowan/|title=Doctor In The House: with John Cowan|date=March 19, 2020|website=V3 Magazine|accessdate=June 17, 2020}}</ref> and [[Davidson College]] in 1996. While at Davidson, he played [[college football]] for the [[Davidson Wildcats football]] team as a [[left tackle]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://davidsonwildcats.com/news/2015/10/23/FB_1022151547.aspx|title=Wildcat Football Gameday Central - Marist|website=Davidson College Athletics|accessdate=June 17, 2020}}</ref> He earned his [[Doctor of Medicine]] at the [[Johns Hopkins School of Medicine]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.northwestgeorgianews.com/calhoun_times/john-cowan-announces-his-intent-to-run-for-u-s-congress-district-14/article_bdffe2e8-36d1-11ea-aaa8-9708c0ada000.html|title=John Cowan announces his intent to run for U.S. Congress District 14|first=From staff|last=reports|website=Northwest Georgia News|accessdate=June 17, 2020}}</ref> 

==Career==
Cowan is a [[neurosurgeon]] from [[Rome, Georgia]], who works at [[Harbin Clinic]]. He is also the [[chief executive officer]] of Cortex Toys, a toy distributor based in Rome.<ref name="Northwest">{{Cite web|url=https://www.northwestgeorgianews.com/rome/news/local/cowan-announces-run-for-u-s-rep-seat-taps-locals-mcniece-and-garner-for-his/article_b8cc2e60-36d8-11ea-ba36-2f2737b20c17.html|title=Cowan announces run for U.S. Rep. seat, taps locals McNiece and Garner for his staff|first=John Bailey|last=JBailey@RN-T.com|website=Northwest Georgia News|accessdate=June 17, 2020}}</ref>

After [[Tom Graves]] announced that he wound not seek reelection for {{ushr|GA|14}} in the [[United States House of Representatives]] in the [[2020 United States House of Representatives elections in Georgia|2020 elections]], Cowan announced his candidacy to succeed him.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.timesfreepress.com/news/local/story/2020/jan/15/rome-neurosurgeenters-race-georgias-14th-cong/513079/|title=Rome neurosurgeon enters race for Georgia's 14th Congressional District|website=timesfreepress.com|accessdate=June 17, 2020}}</ref> In the [[nonpartisan blanket primary]], Cowan received 21% of the vote, finishing in second place behind [[Marjorie Taylor Greene]]. Cowan and Greene advanced to a [[runoff election]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ajc.com/news/gen-politics/election-2020-14th-district-republicans-cowan-greene-headed-for-runoff/5rWYWzYN5d18A6B193XBQP/|title=Election 2020: 14th district Republicans Cowan, Greene headed for a runoff|first=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|last=Sarah Kallis|website=ajc|accessdate=June 17, 2020}}</ref> which Greene won, 57% to 43%.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/marjorie-greene-vs-john-cowan-georgia-14th-district-runoff-results-2020-8|title=Marjorie Greene defeats John Cowan in the runoff for Georgia's 14th congressional district|first=Grace|last=Panetta|website=Business Insider}}</ref> In 2021, Cowan acknowledged that he was considering running against Greene in the 2022 elections.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/former-political-opponent-of-rep-marjorie-taylor-greene-speaks-out|title=Former political opponent of Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene speaks out|date=February 2, 2021|publisher=FOX 5 Atlanta|website=FOX 5 Atlanta}}</ref>

In February 2026, after [[Barry Loudermilk]] announced that he would retire from the House, Cowan announced that he would run to succeed him in representing {{ushr|GA|11}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.northwestgeorgianews.com/rome/news/local/dr-john-cowan-announces-bid-for-loudermilks-u-s-house-seat/article_42f7eaa2-50e3-4efe-9b50-343fa597f817.html|title=Dr. John Cowan announces bid for Loudermilk's U.S. House seat|first=Staff and wire|last=reports|date=February 9, 2026|website=Northwest Georgia News}}</ref> Cowan won the nomination by defeating Rob Adkerson, Loudermilk's former chief of staff, in a runoff election.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wabe.org/cowan-wins-republican-primary-for-barry-loudermilks-us-house-seat-in-georgia/|title=Cowan wins Republican primary for Barry Loudermilk's US House seat in Georgia|first=Melissa|last=Feito|date=June 17, 2026}}</ref> He won the November general election.<ref>https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6188827-cowan-wins-georgia-11th-district/</ref>

==Personal life==
Cowan's wife, Annie is an anesthesiologist.<ref name="Northwest"/>
